title: Three-dimensional generalized-Maxwell relaxation patch
purpose: Verify that the public viscoelastic Study lowers to global equilibrium while retaining exact branch history, energy accounting, temperature shift, rollback, restart and standard field output.

execution.evidence: A homogeneous cube is ramped to one percent axial strain and held. The global finite-element stress is compared with the closed-form generalized-Maxwell response after the ramp and hold; split restart and uninterrupted paths are compared exactly.

observables: Volume-averaged axial stress after a linear strain ramp.
Volume-averaged axial stress after a subsequent constant-strain hold.
Committed Prony-branch state and displacement after checkpoint/restart.
Recoverable energy, cumulative viscous dissipation and constitutive energy residual.
Temperature consumed by an optional WLF or Arrhenius shift law.
acceptance: The global ramp and hold stresses must match the exact uniaxial generalized-Maxwell solution.
Stress must decrease during the constant-strain hold and viscous dissipation must remain nonnegative.
Constitutive work must close against stored energy plus cumulative dissipation to floating-point tolerance.
A split serial checkpoint path must reproduce uninterrupted displacement, stress, state and energy histories.
Serial and two-rank global equilibrium must recover the same exact relaxation stress.
Regional materials must be lowered to one complete quadrature material map without losing region identity.
A changed temperature, material, amplitude, time grid or quadrature identity must invalidate restart.
The common result must expose quadrature and recovered cell S, E, SENER, VDENER and MISES fields plus RF.

quantities.name: mean_axial_stress_after_ramp
quantities.description: E0=1000, E_infinity=600, one branch E1=400, tau=1, strain ramps linearly from 0 to 0.01 over one time unit.

quantities.name: mean_axial_stress_after_hold
quantities.description: The ramp state is held at strain 0.01 for one further time unit.

limitations: This is a homogeneous analytical patch and not an independent external structural benchmark.
The first global provider is three-dimensional, quasi-static and small-strain; this particular patch uses a fixed physical-time grid.
Nonlinear finite-strain viscoelasticity, physical aging, direct harmonic assembly and distributed portable restart are not verified here.
